reading.body:
Verizon's AI lobbying footprint is five filings, sixteen named lobbyists, and six bills, all routed through one registered firm.

The pattern is concentration of effort rather than breadth. Five filings carry sixteen lobbyists, and eleven of those lobbyists appear on four or five filings each. A small core works the account repeatedly while five others appear once. The six bills named are all Senate or House measures from the 2025 session or later, so the activity is current and legislative rather than agency-focused.

For AI specifically, this is a telecommunications company treating AI as a policy file it needs standing coverage on, not a one-off comment. Telecom firms sit between the compute buildout and the network that carries it, and the bills named here are the kind of text that can touch both. The filings do not say which provisions Verizon supported or opposed, and they do not say whether the subject was AI in general or AI as it applies to a specific service.

What the data does not cover is large. Five filings is a count of reports, not of spending, staff time, or influence. The bill numbers are listed without titles or subjects, so a reader cannot tell what any of them would do. The filings name the client and the lobbyists but not the positions argued, and the source note is explicit that a filing records that an issue was lobbied, not the side taken. Nothing here establishes that this activity changed any outcome.

summary: VERIZON COMMUNICATIONS INC. AND VARIOUS SUBSIDIARIES filed 5 Lobbying Disclosure Act reports on AI held by this site. Its clients, the lobbyists named on those filings and the AI bills they name are below. LDA registrant id 5836.
